# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

## Admin

- Re-provision / refresh node-2 (idempotent): `scripts/buildhost/provision.sh` (ships the
  primary's exact Node toolchain to `/opt/nxeon-build/node`, re-applies slices, datasets, mirror,
  Postgres). Run it after upgrading Node on the primary — promotes refuse a version mismatch.
- Release build log on node-2: `/tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/build.log`.

# Cyrus v6: efficiency (cheaper mod generation, same quality)

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-efficiency` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-efficiency`). Service 0.5 patch to
`services/modbuilder/`, NOT deployed. Docs: DOCUMENTATION.md "AI Mod Builder: efficiency (service 0.5)".
Raw analysis output: `spend-2026-10-08.txt` (this folder).

## Method

- Read-only copy of the 138 `build.json` records on VM 88001 and the 4 Claude CLI session transcripts that
  still exist in the container (`tar` over ssh / `docker exec ... tar`; nothing on the VM was changed).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/spend.py` (new) over that copy. Prices: list prices (Sonnet 5 / 5.5 $2 in / $10 out,
  Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, Opus 5 $5/$25, Opus 5.5 $4/$20; cache read 0.1x input; cache write 1.25x (5 min) or 2x (1 h)).
- **No real builds were run (0 of the 6 allowed).** 0.5 can only run for real on VM 88001, which agents must not
  modify, and the AI credential must not be copied to node-2. Submitting builds to the live 0.4 service would not
  have measured anything new. So every "after" number below is an offline cost model, marked "est.".
- Quality gate offline: 29 unit / offline-pipeline tests (real `server.js`, fake CLI + javac), `tsc` clean. The
  real eval (`eval/run_eval.py v6`, ~$3) is the owner's step after deploy (install notes in the docs).

## Where the money goes today

Baseline = eval run v5 (the current default route, Sonnet 5.5, 30 builds, 28 succeeded, 0 repairs): **$0.098 / build**.

| Part | $ / build | Share | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output tokens | $0.060 | 61% | ~4.0k tokens of code that lands in files + ~2.4k other (thinking, text) |
| Cache writes | $0.033 | 33% | everything the model generated, written back to the cache at the **1 h TTL price (2x input)** |
| Cache reads | $0.006 | 6% | the ~15k-token cached prefix + history, re-read each request |
| Uncached input | ~0 | 0% | the prefix cache already works across builds |

Findings:
1. **Prompt caching already works.** First request of every build reads ~14.8k cached tokens (tools + system
   prompt + version sheet + rules); the system prompt is byte-identical per version. Nothing to gain there.
2. **The CLI writes the cache with the 1-hour TTL.** Only 2x pricing reproduces the reported cost (5 min model:
   $2.57 vs reported $2.94 for v5; 1 h: $2.94). That makes cache writes a third of the bill.
3. **Thinking is the biggest variable cost**: ~37-44% of Sonnet 5.5 output, ~71% on the Saka tier (Sonnet 5, avg
   $0.49 per fresh build, n=2, up to 31k thinking tokens in a single planning request), ~77% on Haiku. Thinking also
   gets written to and re-read from the cache during the tool loop, so it costs ~1.4x its output price.
4. **One file per request on the tiers**: the Saka and Katara transcripts wrote one file per API request (11 writing
   requests in one build), each re-reading the whole context. Sonnet 5.5 auto builds already batch (2-3 requests).
5. **Exploration turn**: a fresh build spent its first request on a `Glob` of the empty template folder (1 of the 2 fresh transcripts; the change-request transcript did the same before reading).
6. **Repairs are now rare** (2% of all spend; 0 in v5). Of the 13 historic builds that needed one, 7 failed only on
   mechanical things (final main class x2, import from the wrong package x2, Attribute prefix x3).
7. The Haiku "cheap first repair" really is cheap ($0.010-$0.021), even though switching model loses the cache
   (thinking is not carried across user turns, so the history it must re-cache is small, ~8k tokens).

## Savings table

| # | Lever | Status | Saving | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Saka tier -> Sonnet 5.5** (`MB_TIER_SAKA=claude-sonnet-5-5`, env only) | knob exists; **owner decision** | **~50% on Saka builds** (more on big ones) | measured: 0.3 eval, same 28 prompts, Sonnet 5 $0.203 -> 5.5 $0.104, first try 93% -> 100% |
| 2 | Effort (`MB_EFFORT=medium` for Sonnet/Opus; same value for every call of a build) | implemented, **off** | est. 15-20% if medium halves thinking | model: thinking ~$0.034 of $0.098 incl. its cache cost; unmeasured quality -> eval first |
| 3 | Cache TTL 5 min (`MB_CACHE_TTL=5m`) | implemented, **off** | est. 12% per build **only above ~15 builds/hour on the same version + model**; costs more below that | model: body cache writes 8.1k tokens x (2 - 1.25) x $2/M = $0.012; cold 15k prefix re-write $0.0375 at 5m vs $0.06 at 1h (Poisson break-even ~13-15/h) |
| 4 | Fresh builds: Read/Write/Edit only + "folder holds only the Gradle files" | implemented, **on** | est. 1-5% (a whole request when the model would have Globbed; ~1k fewer cached prefix tokens per request) | transcripts: first request was a Glob in 1 of the 2 fresh builds (the other read its reference image, as told); ~$0.005-0.007 each |
| 5 | Batching instructions (several Writes per response, never one per response; Reads together on changes; small Edits) | implemented, **on** | est. 0-3% on Sonnet 5.5 auto; 10-20% on Saka/Katara if followed | model: 11 single-file requests re-read ~300k cached tokens ($0.06) where 3 would read ~75k |
| 6 | Deterministic auto-fixes before a model repair (`autofix.js`) | implemented, **on** | est. 0-2% average; per affected build saves one repair ($0.01-$0.15) and 10-60 s | 7 of 13 historic repairs; also stops the pre-check's import rules spending a model turn (found by the offline pipeline test) |
| 7 | Repair turn cap 25 (`MB_MAX_TURNS_REPAIR`) | implemented, **on** | tail only | no repair in the records used > 8 |
| 8 | Exact-repeat reuse (`MB_DEDUPE=on`) | implemented, **off** | 100% of a repeated build | records: 15 repeats / 8% of spend, but those are eval re-runs, not customers; `dedupeKey` is now recorded on every build to measure the real rate |
| 9 | Yakko -> Opus 5.5 (`--build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION>=2.1.280`, `MB_TIER_YAKKO=claude-opus-5-5`) | Dockerfile arg added, **off** | est. 20% per token (list price) | Opus 5.5 defaults to effort medium: pin `MB_EFFORT` and eval before switching |

Combined, with only the default-on items (4-7): est. 2-8% on the default route, more on the tiers. The big money
is in decisions 1-3, which change model, effort or cache behaviour and so need the owner and/or the eval.

## Deliberately not done (protects quality, or does not pay)

- **Retrieving only the relevant cheat-sheet sections.** The whole sheet is ~4k tokens, cached, read at $0.20/M:
  about $0.002-$0.008 per build. Slicing it per request makes the prefix vary (more cache writes, which cost 20x
  a read), and a missed section is exactly the failure the sheets fixed (first try 89% -> 100% on 1.21.1). The
  research agent's CloudAPIBench note agrees: retrieval helps rare APIs, can hurt common ones. Keep it whole;
  revisit only for games whose packs are much bigger, and only with an eval.
- **Cheap planner + focused coder.** The planner's output does not remove the coder's own thinking, it adds a call
  with its own prefix, a wrong plan caps quality, and on the customer tiers it would change the model the customer
  chose. Effort (#2) is the same lever inside one model and one cache namespace.
- **A fresh, targeted repair session (only the failing file + error).** The resumed session already has the files
  in context and reads them from cache at 0.1x; a fresh session must write them to the cache again at 1.25-2x and
  loses the other files' context. Repairs are already targeted (errors + API lookup only, 8k cap).
- **Inlining the old source into change prompts.** Claude Code's Edit requires a prior Read of the file, so inlined
  files are read again anyway.
- **Changing effort or model per stage inside one build** (e.g. low effort for repairs): either invalidates the
  prompt cache; not worth it for a 1-2 request repair. The existing Haiku first repair stays (measured cheap).
- **Template library of building blocks the model composes.** Code in files is ~$0.04 per build; boilerplate is a
  fraction of that, and a library the model must learn (and that must be javap-verified per version and shaded
  per plugin) adds risk. Designed below as an eval experiment, not built.
- **Tool-output truncation.** Tool results here are tiny (Write acks, Glob lists); Reads on change requests are the
  files the model must see. Nothing to cut.
- **Lower generate turn cap.** Typical is 2-6 requests; the $2.50/call and $4/build budgets already bound the tail.

## Where the cost-versus-quality line sits (recommendation)

1. Take the free wins now: deploy 0.5 as is (items 4-7 on, everything else off) and run the v6 eval. Pass = 28/28,
   13/13 runtime, 2/2 refused, first try not below v5.
2. Move Saka to Sonnet 5.5. It was measured cheaper, faster and better; this is the single largest saving.
3. Then one bounded effort eval: v6 prompts at `MB_EFFORT=medium` vs default (about $3 per run, 2 runs). Adopt
   medium only if success, first try and runtime are unchanged; otherwise stay. Never go below medium for codegen.
4. Leave the cache TTL at the CLI default until traffic is above ~15 builds/hour per version + model; when the
   service moves from the subscription token to an API key, check the spend split again (the CLI's default TTL may
   differ) and pin `MB_CACHE_TTL=1h` while traffic is low.
5. Turn on `MB_DEDUPE` only after deciding what a reused build costs the customer (today it would be 0 tokens)
   and after `dedupeKey` shows real repeats (template chips are the likely source).

## For the economy agent (`lib/cyrus/estimate.ts`, `cyrus_tok_*`) - not changed here

The token charge is already the measured `costUsd`, so margins hold automatically; only the **estimates** drift:
- `BASE` usd ranges are anchored on Phase 0 Sonnet 5 ($0.28 avg). If Saka moves to Sonnet 5.5, change to roughly
  simple [0.05, 0.10], standard [0.08, 0.16], complex [0.15, 0.30] (eval 0.3: $0.066 / $0.102 / $0.189; v5
  complex max $0.24). If Saka stays on Sonnet 5, the current ranges fit (Saka measured $0.30 and $0.68).
- `costFactor`: katara 0.5 is low against Sonnet 5.5 (Haiku auto $0.066 vs 5.5 $0.098 = ~0.7); yakko 1.7 is low
  (one Opus 5 SimpleHeal cost $0.341, ~5x a simple Sonnet 5.5 build; n=1, so use ~3 until more data).
- Reserve table (`cyrus_tok_reserve_table`): same direction as `BASE`.
- With `MB_DEDUPE=on`, a reused build reports `costUsd` 0 and settles 0 tokens (`tokensForCost` returns 0 for 0).

## Knowledge packs: how the Minecraft sheets and rules map to GameSupport `knowledge`

`node services/modbuilder/tools/export-knowledge.js` prints them in the contract's shape now (1.21.1: 43 sheet
lines / 13 rules; 1.21.4: 42/15; 1.21.8: 42/16; 1.21.11: 42/17):
- `apiSheet` = one line per bullet of `sheets/<ver>.md`, prefixed by its section (`[Attributes] ...`), so a
  retriever can select by tag. The sheet stays generated by `gen-sheets.py` (javap-checked); do not hand-edit.
- `failureRules[]`: `id` <- id; `detect` <- `pattern` (source regex the pre-check runs) or `warning:<regex>` for
  rules that only show up as a compiler warning ("" = prompt-only lesson); `fix` <- `fix` (with `$1` capture
  placeholders) or `rule`; `why` <- `rule` + the build ids it was mined from (+ "main class only" for `scope`).
- Gaps in the contract worth adding: `knowledge` holds one `version`, but a game supports several (Minecraft: 4)
  -> make it `knowledge?: Pack[]` or a map by version; rules need `versions?: string[]` (one rule covers several),
  `scope?: "main"|"any"`, and `kind?: "source"|"compiler-warning"|"runtime"` instead of the `warning:` prefix;
  optional `autofix?: {replace: string}` for purely mechanical rules (what `autofix.js` does from the jar).
- Single source of truth: the build service runs JS inside its image and cannot import TS GameSupport. Keep each
  game's pack as JSON next to its build service (like `rules/failure-rules.json`) and have `lib/cyrus/games/<id>.ts`
  import or generate from it, rather than two copies.
- Retrieval: keep injecting the whole pack while it is a few thousand tokens (cached, see above). If a game's pack
  grows past ~10k tokens, select lines by section tag from the request + plan, put the selection AFTER the cached
  prefix (user turn), and gate it behind the eval.

## Template library (designed, not built)

Verified blocks (command executor + tab complete, config with reload, YAML data store, scheduler/cooldowns,
InventoryHolder menu, MiniMessage helper) in a fixed package `dev.nxeon.mb.lib`, pre-placed in the workspace and
listed (API only, ~500 tokens) in the cached system prompt. After the model finishes, the service deletes unused
blocks and relocates the used ones into the plugin's own package (no class clashes between plugins). Each block
javap-checked per version. Expected saving: part of the ~$0.04 code output on menu/data-heavy plugins. Ship only
if a v6-vs-blocks eval shows equal success, first try and runtime.

## Files and commits

`services/modbuilder/{server.js, usage.js (new), autofix.js (new), prompts.js, precheck.js, run.sh, Dockerfile,
tools/spend.py (new), tools/export-knowledge.js (new)}`, `test/modbuilder-efficiency.test.ts`,
`test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

# Advanced mods for the six Cyrus games: how professionals build them, and what Cyrus should add

Research write-up for the Cyrus v6 programme. Compiled 2026-10-08. Research only: no repo changes, no purchases, no sign-ups.

Source tags used throughout:
- **[V]** verified this session from a primary source (official docs, the project's own repo or API, a licence text).
- **[S]** secondary (hosting-provider knowledge bases, news, aggregators, search snippets). Plausible, but re-check before anyone relies on it.
- **[L]** verified locally in the Nxeon repo, the build service or the owner's handoff.
- **[I]** inference or general expert knowledge that was not checked this session.

AI reliability ratings used in each game section:
- **R1** reliable today with guardrails (templates, API sheets, compile and validate loop).
- **R2** works only with an automated verification step plus, for some requests, human review.
- **R3** needs a human (design judgement, binary tooling, or assets the AI cannot author).

---

## 1. Executive summary (one page)

**What "advanced" means.** In every game the same ladder shows up. Rung 1 is configuration and data edits. Rung 2 is scripted behaviour (commands, events, simple GUIs). Rung 3 is new content (items, mobs, recipes, quests). Rung 4 is new systems (economies, minigames, world generation, custom AI). Rung 5 is engine-level work (patching game code, custom assets, cooked packages). AI is good on rungs 1 to 3 and decent on rung 4 where the platform has a high-level API. Rung 5 is mostly a human job.

**The finding that matters most: version drift, not cleverness, is what breaks AI-written mods.**
- Cyrus's own Minecraft build service already learned this. Its reviewed failure-rule file holds 18 rules, and nearly all are API names that changed between Paper versions (`Attribute.GENERIC_*` vs unprefixed, `Material.GRASS`, boats split per wood, `EntityType.POTION` removed) [L: `services/modbuilder/rules/failure-rules.json`].
- Every other game moved under modders' feet in the last 90 days: Palworld 1.0 (2026-07-10), Terraria 1.4.5 (2026-01-27 [S]) which tModLoader does not yet ship for, Valheim 1.0 (2026-09-09, "piece categories overhauled", Jotunn rewritten for 1.0.7), Project Zomboid Build 42.20 stable (2026-07-29), Rust's monthly Thursday update. Training data for these games is mostly pre-change.
- Published evidence agrees: version-controllable code generation is "a significant challenge, even for GPT-4o" ([VersiCode](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07411)); valid calls to low-frequency APIs were 38.6% for GPT-4o, rising to 47.9% with documentation retrieval, and badly chosen retrieval cut high-frequency accuracy by 39 points ([CloudAPIBench / DAG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.09726)); and compile-pass rate can be anti-correlated with functional correctness ([Mage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07342)).

**Honest AI assessment by game (today).**

| Game | Best-supported "advanced" targets | Needs a human |
|---|---|---|
| Minecraft Paper/Purpur | Commands, GUIs, economies, quests, minigames, admin tooling, custom items via data components (R1 to R2) | World-gen tuning, balance, custom blocks, resource-pack art, Folia-safe rewrites (R3) |
| Terraria tModLoader | Items, buffs, recipes, simple NPCs and projectiles (R1 to R2) | Bosses, tiles, world gen, netcode edge cases, IL patching (R3) |
| Terraria TShock | Server commands, permissions, anti-grief, events (R1 to R2) | Anything needing new items or art (impossible server-only) |
| Valheim (BepInEx + Jotunn) | Config and stat changes, clone-and-modify items, recipes, status effects (R1 to R2) | New models and prefabs (Unity editor), new biomes (R3) |
| Rust (Oxide/Carbon) | Kits, teleports, shops, custom UI, anti-cheat tooling (R1 to R2) | New items or models (impossible server-side), monthly-update triage (needs monitoring) |
| Palworld | PalSchema JSON data mods (R2) | UE4SS Lua without an SDK dump, Blueprint LogicMods, cooked assets (R3) |
| Project Zomboid | Item/recipe scripts and small Lua (R2, once B42 golden examples exist) | Models, maps, anything mixing B41 knowledge (R3) |

**Three hard platform facts Cyrus should surface to customers**
1. **Palworld server-side mods are Windows-server only** per community docs quoting the official docs [S: [XGamingServer](https://xgamingserver.com/docs/palworld/mod-installation), [ConnectHosting](https://connecthosting.net/blog/palworld-server-mods-what-works), [gamever.io](https://gamever.io/knowledge-base/server-side-mods-in-palworld-palmodsettingsini-and-the-flag-that-undoes-everything)]. Nxeon's Palworld image is the native Linux server (config path `.../Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini`) [L: `lib/game-control.ts:239`]. Unless that is wrong, most Palworld mods cannot run on Nxeon's Palworld servers today. This must be checked before the Palworld agent's `side` and `reason` strings are written.
2. **tModLoader and TShock cannot be combined**: tModLoader stable (v2026.08.3.0) targets Terraria 1.4.4; TShock 6.2.1 targets Terraria 1.4.5.8 [V: GitHub release APIs]. tModLoader has an active `1.4.5` branch (last commit 2026-10-07) [V], so this will change; Cyrus's version table must treat them as two products.
3. **Rust and Palworld-style "new item" ideas cannot be delivered server-side.** Vanilla Rust clients only show existing prefabs and Facepunch-approved workshop skins [S]. Cyrus should refuse or reframe those requests honestly.

**What Cyrus should add (ranked; details in section 9).**
1. Per-game **version-and-API knowledge packs** generated from the real jars, SDKs and docs, injected only for the target version (the Minecraft "sheets plus failure rules" pattern, generalised). Highest value, medium effort per game.
2. A **structured spec card** (commands, permissions, configs, GUIs, acceptance tests) before code, shared by all games. It also feeds tests.
3. **Golden examples** per game, human-verified and compile-tested, retrieved by nearest match. These double as regression tests.
4. **Multi-file projects with typed file roles** (code, config, data, lang, assets) and diff-based edits.
5. A **verification ladder** per game (static lint, compile, unit tests of pure logic, live smoke test on a throwaway server where the game allows).
6. **Dependency handling** (declared soft-dependencies, compile-only API digests, install-time "requires X" warnings).
7. **Iterative refinement from real server logs**, then multi-step planning for large mods, then companion asset packs (see `RENDERS-AND-TEXTURES.md`).

---

## 2. Method and limits

- Primary sources were fetched with WebFetch or `curl`, plus the GitHub, Thunderstore and Hugging Face APIs, which were reachable. umod.org, pzwiki.net and pzfans.com sit behind Cloudflare challenges; I did not try to bypass them. Where a fact would have come from them, it is tagged [S] and sourced from alternatives (Carbon's MIT-licensed docs repo, a community Build 42 guide, hosting-provider docs).
- `WebFetch` summarises pages with a small model. Facts that mattered were cross-checked against raw files or APIs where possible (release APIs, raw wiki markdown, licence texts). Anything only seen in a summary is tagged [S].
- Dates and version numbers are from release APIs read on 2026-10-08 unless noted.
- Effort figures in section 9 are my estimates for one engineer using AI assistance [I]. They are not measured.
## 4. Minecraft: Paper and Purpur

### 4.1 Platform snapshot
- **Paper** is GPL-3.0 [prior research, [V] at the time]; **Purpur** is "a drop-in replacement for Paper servers designed for configurability, new fun and exciting gameplay features, and performance" [V: [Purpur README](https://github.com/PurpurMC/Purpur)]. Purpur plugins use the Paper API, so Cyrus can target Paper and run on both.
- Version lines in Cyrus today: 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11 [L: `MB_VERSIONS`]. Paper and Purpur also publish a 26.x line (Javadocs exist for 26.2) [V: [Paper 26.2 javadocs](https://jd.papermc.io/paper/26.2/org/bukkit/generator/package-use.html), Purpur README branch badge `ver/26.2`]. The service's Java 21 toolchain would need Java 25 for 26.x [prior research].
- **Side**: server-only. Vanilla clients can join. Custom visuals need a server-sent resource pack: `resource-pack` URL, `resource-pack-sha1`, `resource-pack-id`, `require-resource-pack`, a prompt; pack size limit 250 MiB [V: [Minecraft Wiki server.properties](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server.properties)]. Since 1.20.3 a server can stack several packs and remove them individually [S: [Paper Adventure docs](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/resource-pack/)].
- Hot reload: not safely. Needs a restart or a plugin-manager reload (risky). `/reload` is discouraged [I].

### 4.2 What "advanced" looks like, and how professionals do it

| Capability | Professional technique | Libraries / APIs | AI today |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Custom items** with new looks and behaviour | Stack data components (`item_model`, `custom_model_data`, tool, food, lore, enchantments) on a base item, store identity in PDC, ship a resource pack | Paper Data Component API, PDC, Recipes API [V: [data components](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/data-component-api/), [PDC](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/pdc/), [recipes](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/recipes/)] | R1 for stats and behaviour, R2 when it needs a pack (art is R3) |
| **Custom blocks** | There are no truly new blocks on a vanilla client. Pros emulate with note-block states, tripwire, or display entities, and use Nexo or ItemsAdder to manage packs | Nexo docs, display entities [S: [Nexo FAQ](https://docs.nexomc.com/general-usage/faq/itemmodels-vs.-custommodeldata)] | R2/R3 (mining-speed emulation, drops, anti-dupe are fiddly) |
| **GUIs** | Inventory menus with strict click, drag and shift-click handling; 1.21.6+ Dialog API for forms (text input, sliders, dropdowns, confirm dialogs) | triumph-gui, InvUI (MIT) [prior], Dialog API [V: [dialogs](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/dialogs/)] | R1 simple, R2 complex (dupe edge cases) |
| **Commands** | Brigadier via the lifecycle API, registered in a bootstrapper so datapack functions can see them; Cloud or ACF in older stacks | Paper Command API, Incendo Cloud (MIT) [V: [lifecycle](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/lifecycle/)] | R1 (but see the 4.5 note about Cyrus's current `plugin.yml`-only rule) |
| **Custom enchantments, biomes, registries** | Registry API at server bootstrap with `compose` and `entryAdd` lifecycle events | Paper Registry API [V: [registries](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/registries/)]: marked experimental; exceptions during bootstrap shut the server down | R3 for now |
| **Custom mob behaviour** | Add or replace AI goals with the Mob Goals API; use the Pathfinder for movement | `Goal`, `GoalKey`, `MobGoals` [V: [mob goals](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/mob-goals/)] | R2 |
| **NPCs** | Citizens with custom Traits, or packet NPCs; dialogue trees from data files | Citizens API [V: [Citizens wiki](https://wiki.citizensnpcs.co/API)] | R2 |
| **AI-driven NPCs** (LLM dialogue) | Async HTTP to an LLM, never on the main thread; per-player rate limits and cost caps; moderation on input and output; fallback lines; prompts held server-side | Bukkit async scheduler; Mindcraft (MIT, 5.8k stars) shows the agent side [V: [mindcraft repo](https://github.com/mindcraft-bots/mindcraft)] | R2; Cyrus's safety scan currently **blocks all networking**, so this needs a deliberate "Connector" design (section 9) |
| **World generation** | `ChunkGenerator` with separate noise, surface, caves and bedrock steps, plus `BiomeProvider`; they take `WorldInfo`, not `World`, because `World` calls can deadlock during generation [S: [Bukkit/CraftBukkit change notes](https://hub.spigotmc.org/jenkins/view/RSS/job/CraftBukkit-RSS/2198/)]. Datapack worldgen JSON is the safer route | `org.bukkit.generator` [V: Javadoc index] | R2 for datapack JSON, R3 for tuned noise |
| **Economies** | Vault or VaultUnlocked as the abstraction so shops and jobs plugins interoperate [S: [Vault explainer](https://mineguard.pro/en/blog/vault-plugin-economy-permissions-explained)]; balances as integers (cents) or `BigDecimal`; async persistence with write-behind caching; transaction logging | Vault API, SQLite/MariaDB with a pool [I] | R1 basic, R2 with races; **balance design is R3** |
| **Minigames and arenas** | State machine per match, arena templates copied per game, cleanup on quit, kick, death and match end | Scoreboard API (broken on Folia [V]) | R2 |
| **Quests** | Data-driven YAML/JSON quest definitions, event listeners, PDC progress | Configurate (Apache-2.0) [prior] | R1 |
| **Performance mods** | Limit entities and chunk ticking, batch work, move I/O off-thread; measure with a profiler such as spark [I] | Paper scheduler [V: [scheduler](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/scheduler/)] | R2: claims of "faster" must be measured, which Cyrus cannot do today |
| **Admin tooling** | Audit logs, rollback, moderation GUIs, Discord bridges (needs network) | Plugin messaging, PDC | R1 to R2 |

### 4.3 Techniques that separate advanced plugins from tutorial plugins
1. **Item identity in PDC, not names or lore.** PDC survives renames and persists to disk; names and lore collide with players' anvils [V: [PDC](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/pdc/)]. The API also warns that data components may break across Minecraft versions, unlike `ItemMeta` [V].
2. **Item models over CustomModelData override stacks.** From 1.21.4 an `item_model` points at an items definition under `assets/<namespace>/items/`, so packs no longer fight over vanilla model overrides [V: [Nexo](https://docs.nexomc.com/general-usage/faq/itemmodels-vs.-custommodeldata), [Items model definition](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Items_model_definition)]. Supporting clients older than 1.21.4 still needs CMD overrides.
3. **Bootstrap-time registration** when the feature must exist before worlds load (commands for datapack functions, registry entries). Requires `paper-plugin.yml`, with classloader isolation: plugins cannot see each other's classes unless `join-classpath` is set [V: [Paper plugins](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/getting-started/paper-plugins/)].
4. **Libraries via the Paper loader**: `MavenLibraryResolver` instead of shading everything. The docs advise against Maven Central directly and recommend Paper's mirror [V].
5. **Tests**: MockBukkit (MIT) for unit tests of commands and events, mineflayer bots for live behaviour [prior research]. MockBukkit builds a ByteBuddy proxy of your main class, so a `final` main class breaks every test [prior local experiment].
6. **Folia awareness** only when asked. Folia has no main thread; plugins must declare `folia-supported: true` and use region, entity, global and async schedulers; `Entity#teleport` never returns (use `teleportAsync`); the scoreboard API is broken [V: [Folia support](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/folia-support/), [Folia wiki](https://github.com/PaperMC/Folia/wiki/Plugin-Compatibility)].

### 4.4 Pitfalls
- Touching world, entities or inventories from async code. Keep async for I/O, hop back to the main thread to apply results [S: skill pages consistent with Paper docs].
- Long-lived maps keyed by `Player`. Key by UUID; clear on quit, kick, death and match end [S].
- Saving in `onDisable` through the async scheduler: the scheduler refuses new tasks while the plugin disables, so the data is lost [L: rule `ondisable-sync-save`].
- `BukkitRunnable` passed to `runTask*` throws at runtime [L: rule `scheduler-bukkitrunnable`].
- Declaring `isEnabled()`/`getServer()` in the main class: `JavaPlugin` defines them as final [L].
- API drift: `Attribute` is an enum on 1.21.1 and an interface on 1.21.4+; `Particle`, `PotionEffectType` and `Enchantment` constants were renamed [L]. These are exactly what an API sheet per version catches.
- Inventory GUI duplication via drag, number-key and hopper interactions [I].

### 4.5 Performance and compatibility
- Paper vs Purpur: Purpur adds config and gameplay options; its extra API is not in Paper, so Cyrus output should target the Paper API and avoid Purpur-only calls unless the customer picked Purpur [I].
- Folia is a different product: most plugins do not run on it unless rewritten [V].
- Current Cyrus constraints in the build service system prompt [L: `prompts.js`] that matter for "advanced": only Paper API + JDK on the classpath (no Vault, ProtocolLib, LuckPerms API); `plugin.yml` plus `getCommand().setExecutor` only (no Brigadier, no lifecycle events, no `registerCommand`); no networking of any kind; no reflection; single plugin per build. These are sound for safety and reliability, and they are the main ceiling on "advanced". Section 9 proposes controlled relaxations.

### 4.6 What AI can and cannot do (Minecraft)
- **R1:** commands, listeners, config-driven features, simple GUIs, quests from data, many admin tools. Compile-and-scan catches most failures.
- **R2:** custom items with resource packs, economies, minigames, mob goals, datapack worldgen. Needs spec confirmation, tests and a live smoke test.
- **R3:** economy balance and game feel, world-gen tuning, custom blocks, Folia migration, resource-pack art, performance claims.
- Nothing in Paper adds new blocks or items on a vanilla client; say so plainly in the UI [prior research].

---

# Nxeon Mod Builder build service.
# Base: claudebox (node 22 + Claude Code CLI + iptables egress allowlist).
FROM claudebox:14f689d

USER root
# Optional (0.5): pin a newer Claude Code CLI than the base image ships (2.1.241), e.g.
#   docker build --build-arg CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.280 ...   (needed for Opus 5.5 on Yakko).
# Empty = keep the base image's CLI (the tested default). Verify /health + one build after changing it.
ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=""
RUN if [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION" ]; then npm install -g --no-audit --no-fund "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" && claude --version; fi
ARG MC_VERSIONS="1.21.11 1.21.8 1.21.4 1.21.1"

# Pinned toolchain (Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 + Gradle 8.14.3), copied in from the
# Nxeon research toolchain so the image never depends on a moving download.
COPY toolchain.tgz /tmp/toolchain.tgz
RUN mkdir -p /opt/mb && tar xzf /tmp/toolchain.tgz -C /opt/mb && rm /tmp/toolchain.tgz \
 && ln -s /opt/mb/jdk-21.0.12.1+1 /opt/mb/jdk && ln -s /opt/mb/gradle-8.14.3 /opt/mb/gradle
ENV JAVA_HOME=/opt/mb/jdk
ENV PATH=/opt/mb/jdk/bin:/opt/mb/gradle/bin:$PATH

COPY template /opt/mb/template
COPY package.json /opt/mb/app/package.json
RUN cd /opt/mb/app && npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund && chown -R claude:claude /opt/mb

# Pre-warm the Gradle cache for every supported version and record the exact
# compile classpath. This is the ONLY step that talks to repo.papermc.io /
# repo.maven.apache.org, and it happens at image build time (outside the
# runtime egress firewall). Runtime builds are fully offline.
USER claude
ENV GRADLE_USER_HOME=/opt/mb/gradle-home
RUN set -e; mkdir -p /opt/mb/classpath; for v in $MC_VERSIONS; do \
      gradle --no-daemon -q -p /opt/mb/template writeClasspath -PmcApi=${v}-R0.1-SNAPSHOT -PcpOut=/opt/mb/classpath/${v}.txt; \
      test -s /opt/mb/classpath/${v}.txt; \
    done; rm -rf /opt/mb/template/.gradle /opt/mb/template/build; ls -la /opt/mb/classpath
# Class index per version (every class name on the compile classpath), used by
# precheck.js to turn "cannot find symbol" into "this class lives in package X".
RUN set -e; for v in $MC_VERSIONS; do \
      for j in $(tr ':' ' ' < /opt/mb/classpath/${v}.txt); do jar tf "$j" | grep '\.class$' || true; done | sort -u > /opt/mb/classpath/${v}.classes.txt; \
      test -s /opt/mb/classpath/${v}.classes.txt; \
    done; wc -l /opt/mb/classpath/*.classes.txt

USER root
RUN mkdir -p /work /data && chown claude:claude /work /data
USER claude
COPY --chown=claude:claude server.js scan.js prompts.js route.js precheck.js live.js usage.js autofix.js /opt/mb/app/
COPY --chown=claude:claude sheets /opt/mb/app/sheets
COPY --chown=claude:claude rules /opt/mb/app/rules
ENV MB_VERSIONS="1.21.11 1.21.8 1.21.4 1.21.1"
WORKDIR /data
EXPOSE 3000
ENTRYPOINT ["/bin/bash", "/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["node", "/opt/mb/app/server.js"]
#!/bin/bash
# (Re)create the Mod Builder container on the build VM. Idempotent.
#   /root/claudebox.env   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... (owner subscription)  -- or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... for paid API
#   /root/modbuilder.env  MODBUILDER_API_KEY=...      (bearer key the portal uses)
set -euo pipefail
IMAGE="${1:-modbuilder:0.5}"
# Routing / knowledge knobs (see route.js, prompts.js): passed through when set in the caller's env,
# e.g. MB_ROUTING=off /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3  (or put them in /root/modbuilder.env).
PASS=()
for k in MB_ROUTING MB_CLASSIFIER MB_MODEL_SIMPLE MB_MODEL_STANDARD MB_MODEL_COMPLEX MB_REPAIR_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_FIRST MB_REPAIR_SMALL_MAX MB_ROUTE_SIMPLE_MAX MB_ROUTE_COMPLEX_MIN MB_SHEETS MB_RULES MB_MAX_REPAIRS MB_LIVE_STREAM MB_MAX_TURNS MB_MAX_TURNS_REPAIR MB_AUTOFIX MB_LEAN_TOOLS MB_EFFORT MB_CACHE_TTL MB_DEDUPE MB_DEDUPE_MAX_AGE_H MB_TIER_KATARA MB_TIER_SAKA MB_TIER_YAKKO; do
  if [[ -n "${!k:-}" ]]; then PASS+=(-e "$k=${!k}"); fi
done
docker rm -f modbuilder >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker run -d --name modbuilder --restart unless-stopped \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN \
  --env-file /root/claudebox.env --env-file /root/modbuilder.env \
  -e MB_CONCURRENCY="${MB_CONCURRENCY:-2}" -e MB_MODEL="${MB_MODEL:-sonnet}" ${PASS[@]+"${PASS[@]}"} \
  -p 127.0.0.1:7340:3000 \
  -v /var/lib/modbuilder/data:/data -v /var/lib/modbuilder/work:/work \
  --memory 5g --pids-limit 512 \
  "$IMAGE"
// Nxeon Mod Builder: pinned Paper plugin template.
// The build service compiles with javac against the exact classpath this file
// resolves (see `writeClasspath`), so this file is also how you rebuild locally:
//   gradle build -PmcApi=1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT
plugins { java }

val mcApi: String = (findProperty("mcApi") as String?) ?: "1.21.11-R0.1-SNAPSHOT"

group = "dev.nxeon.plugins"
version = "1.0.0"

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
    maven("https://repo.papermc.io/repository/maven-public/")
}

dependencies {
    compileOnly("io.papermc.paper:paper-api:$mcApi")
}

java { toolchain.languageVersion.set(JavaLanguageVersion.of(21)) }

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.encoding = "UTF-8"
    options.release.set(21)
}

// Used once at image-build time to pre-warm the dependency cache and record
// the resolved compile classpath for each supported Minecraft version.
tasks.register("writeClasspath") {
    val out = (findProperty("cpOut") as String?) ?: "classpath.txt"
    doLast {
        file(out).writeText(configurations.getByName("compileClasspath").resolve().joinToString(":") { it.absolutePath })
    }
}
rootProject.name = "nxeon-plugin"

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
270 /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost

content.thinking:
PaperMC's docs are BSD-2-Clause, so I can adapt code samples from there with proper attribution retaining their copyright notice, and compiling against the Paper API jars themselves is also fine since that's the service's purpose. I'm planning to seed the library mostly with freshly authored Nxeon patterns, supplementing with a few adapted PaperMC doc examples credited accordingly.

I should pull from docs pages like PDC, scheduler, event listeners, and custom InventoryHolder, avoiding Brigadier since the service only supports plugin.yml-based plugins. But I need to think through the real implication of BSD-2's condition 2: if customer plugins bundle derived code as binary jars, they may be obligated to reproduce the copyright notice in their distributed documentation, which could be a genuine compliance burden for every customer plugin built this way.

My instinct is to prefer licenses without output attribution requirements (MIT-0, CC0, Unlicense, 0BSD, Nxeon-authored) for patterns that flow into customer code, and flag BSD-2/MIT/Apache-derived patterns with an `attribution.requiredInOutput` flag so the service can inject a NOTICE file into the jar automatically. Detecting actual usage could rely on fingerprinting pattern content, but a simpler approach may be to keep third-party permissive snippets reference-only and excluded from retrieval until the notice-injection mechanism exists.

I'm deciding the seed set should be 100% Nxeon-authored patterns under a "LicenseRef-Nxeon-Authored" license with customer output rights, treating BSD-2 docs only as factual reference rather than copied code to avoid attribution complexity. Instead of adding token third-party patterns for policy demonstration, I think it's better to build real schema support for third-party sources (spdx, url, commit, attribution text, noticeRequiredInOutput) and have the ingest tool enforce an SPDX allow-list plus retrieval preferences.

For notice generation, I'll skip fragile fingerprint detection in output and instead take a simple, over-inclusive approach: if a pattern requiring notices was injected into the build prompt at all, copy its notice text into a META-INF file before packaging. It's a small addition, legally safe, and keeps scope manageable. I also note MIT-0 examples like Jotunn are Valheim-specific, so I'd need a genuine MIT-0/CC0 example for Minecraft instead.

Now I'm tackling the bigger retrieval design question: how to keep the cached prefix cheap while still allowing per-request variation. My plan splits retrieval into tiers—a byte-identical cached index of all verified patterns per version (compact one-liners with id, title, category, tags, and API classes, costing fractions of a cent per build) and a second tier where up to three full patterns are deterministically selected per request based on keyword/tag matching against the prompt.

The matched pattern bodies get placed in the initial user message, adding roughly 2000 tokens that get written into the cache; this adds about 9% to per-build cost. The real payoff isn't shrinking output tokens since the model still has to write the code, but rather improving quality on rarer APIs and reducing the repair rate, which is where the actual savings should come from.

I'm now weighing a cheaper alternative: storing patterns as on-demand files the model can Read only when needed, with a lightweight index pointing to them in the cached prefix. This costs an extra tool round-trip (~$0.004-0.006) but lets the model choose retrieval selectively rather than always paying for unused patterns — though it conflicts with the existing instruction telling the model never to Read the workspace on fresh builds, so that instruction would need to be modified.

Following the brief's deterministic-first approach, I'm planning to select patterns by matching feature tags from the prompt, injecting only high-confidence top matches while leaving an index for the model to Read others on demand from a dedicated library folder. Since sanitizeWorkspace strips unexpected files noisily, I'll have the service silently remove this library folder before sanitization runs, similar to how dropRefs is handled, and I'll guard against injecting patterns for trivial APIs the model already handles well.

Now I'm distinguishing between common APIs, which stay index-only for on-demand lookup, and rarer, more error-prone patterns like persistent data containers, inventory menus with safe click handling, and versioned Attribute APIs, which get auto-injected when matched. Since some patterns differ across Minecraft versions, I need the schema to support version-specific variants so injected code reliably compiles against whatever versions the project targets.

I'm also thinking through an "attribute-by-key" pattern using Registry.ATTRIBUTE to sidestep the enum-vs-interface drift between versions, which I'll need to compile-verify. Beyond that, I want an offline evaluation: running the deterministic selector against the 30-prompt eval set, measuring injected token counts, and projecting cost deltas to judge whether the injection approach is worth it.

Since I can't access VM 88001's production path or copy the AI credential to node-2, I can't actually run real builds to measure quality impact, so I'll report zero like the efficiency agent did. Instead, I can do an offline substitute: checking the 13 historic build failures against the library's patterns to estimate how many repairs the library would have prevented.

content.content:
# Paper API 1.21.1 cheat sheet
Verified against paper-api-1.21.1-R0.1-SNAPSHOT (the exact jar you compile against). Names here are correct for 1.21.1; do not use names from other versions.

## Attributes (org.bukkit.attribute.Attribute)
- In 1.21.1 `Attribute` is an ENUM and every constant has a GENERIC_/PLAYER_/ZOMBIE_ prefix. Unprefixed names (MAX_HEALTH, SCALE, MOVEMENT_SPEED, ATTACK_DAMAGE...) DO NOT EXIST here.
- Use: GENERIC_MAX_HEALTH, GENERIC_MOVEMENT_SPEED, GENERIC_ATTACK_DAMAGE, GENERIC_ATTACK_SPEED, GENERIC_ARMOR, GENERIC_ARMOR_TOUGHNESS, GENERIC_KNOCKBACK_RESISTANCE, GENERIC_SCALE, GENERIC_JUMP_STRENGTH, GENERIC_GRAVITY, GENERIC_STEP_HEIGHT, GENERIC_SAFE_FALL_DISTANCE, GENERIC_FALL_DAMAGE_MULTIPLIER, GENERIC_FOLLOW_RANGE, GENERIC_FLYING_SPEED, GENERIC_LUCK, PLAYER_BLOCK_BREAK_SPEED, PLAYER_BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE, PLAYER_ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE, PLAYER_SNEAKING_SPEED, ZOMBIE_SPAWN_REINFORCEMENTS.
- Registry keys carry the prefix too: minecraft:generic.scale, minecraft:generic.max_health. `Attribute.valueOf("GENERIC_SCALE")` works (enum).
- `entity.getAttribute(attr)` returns AttributeInstance or null: always null-check. Methods: getBaseValue(), setBaseValue(double), getValue(), getDefaultValue(), addModifier(m), addTransientModifier(m), removeModifier(Key), getModifier(Key), getModifiers().
- Modifiers: `new AttributeModifier(new NamespacedKey(plugin, "growth"), amount, AttributeModifier.Operation.ADD_NUMBER)` (optional 4th arg EquipmentSlotGroup). Operations: ADD_NUMBER, ADD_SCALAR, MULTIPLY_SCALAR_1. The UUID/String constructors are deprecated for removal. Remove the old modifier with `removeModifier(key)` before adding it again with the same key.
- Size changes: the default scale is 1.0; setBaseValue on the scale attribute or use one keyed modifier. Max health: set the attribute first, then `setHealth(Math.min(h, attr.getValue()))`.

## Sounds (org.bukkit.Sound)
- In 1.21.1 `Sound` is an ENUM. Sound.valueOf(name) works.
- e.g. ENTITY_PLAYER_LEVELUP, BLOCK_NOTE_BLOCK_PLING, BLOCK_NOTE_BLOCK_HAT, UI_BUTTON_CLICK, UI_TOAST_CHALLENGE_COMPLETE, ENTITY_EXPERIENCE_ORB_PICKUP, ENTITY_ENDER_DRAGON_GROWL, ENTITY_WITHER_SPAWN, ENTITY_ENDERMAN_TELEPORT, ENTITY_VILLAGER_NO.
- `player.playSound(player.getLocation(), Sound.X, 1f, 1f)`. Version-proof for config strings: `player.playSound(net.kyori.adventure.sound.Sound.sound(Key.key(name), net.kyori.adventure.sound.Sound.Source.MASTER, 1f, 1f))`.

## Particles (org.bukkit.Particle, an enum in every version)
- Old names DO NOT EXIST. Old -> new: REDSTONE->DUST, SPELL_WITCH->WITCH, VILLAGER_HAPPY->HAPPY_VILLAGER, VILLAGER_ANGRY->ANGRY_VILLAGER, SMOKE_NORMAL->SMOKE, SMOKE_LARGE->LARGE_SMOKE, EXPLOSION_NORMAL->POOF, FIREWORKS_SPARK->FIREWORK, ENCHANTMENT_TABLE->ENCHANT, TOTEM->TOTEM_OF_UNDYING, ITEM_CRACK->ITEM, BLOCK_CRACK->BLOCK, SPELL_MOB->ENTITY_EFFECT, CRIT_MAGIC->ENCHANTED_HIT, DRIP_WATER->DRIPPING_WATER. Unchanged: FLAME, HEART, NOTE, CRIT, END_ROD, CLOUD, PORTAL, SOUL_FIRE_FLAME.
- Particles that REQUIRE data (spawning them without it fails at runtime): DUST needs `new Particle.DustOptions(Color.RED, 1.0f)`; DUST_COLOR_TRANSITION needs Particle.DustTransition; ENTITY_EFFECT needs a `Color`; ITEM needs an ItemStack; BLOCK, FALLING_DUST, BLOCK_MARKER, DUST_PILLAR need BlockData (`Material.STONE.createBlockData()`); SCULK_CHARGE needs Float; SHRIEK needs Integer; VIBRATION needs Vibration.
- Particle.Trail and Particle.Spell do not exist in 1.21.1; TRAIL, PALE_OAK_LEAVES, BLOCK_CRUMBLE, FIREFLY are not in 1.21.1.
- `world.spawnParticle(Particle.FLAME, loc, count, offX, offY, offZ, extraSpeed)`; with data: `world.spawnParticle(Particle.DUST, loc, 10, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0, new Particle.DustOptions(Color.AQUA, 1f))`. For a config value use `Particle.valueOf(name.toUpperCase())` inside try/catch.

## Potion effects and enchantments (same names in all 1.21.x)
- PotionEffectType old -> new (old names DO NOT EXIST): INCREASE_DAMAGE->STRENGTH, SLOW->SLOWNESS, FAST_DIGGING->HASTE, SLOW_DIGGING->MINING_FATIGUE, JUMP->JUMP_BOOST, DAMAGE_RESISTANCE->RESISTANCE, HEAL->INSTANT_HEALTH, HARM->INSTANT_DAMAGE, CONFUSION->NAUSEA. Unchanged: SPEED, REGENERATION, FIRE_RESISTANCE, INVISIBILITY, NIGHT_VISION, GLOWING, LEVITATION, SLOW_FALLING.
- `new PotionEffect(PotionEffectType.SPEED, 30 * 20, 1)` = Speed II for 30 s (amplifier 0 = level I). Extra ctor args: (type, ticks, amp, ambient, particles, icon). `PotionEffect.INFINITE_DURATION` exists. `entity.addPotionEffect(effect)`. getByName is deprecated: for config strings use `Registry.EFFECT.get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("speed"))`.
- Enchantment old -> new (old names DO NOT EXIST): DAMAGE_ALL->SHARPNESS, DAMAGE_UNDEAD->SMITE, DAMAGE_ARTHROPODS->BANE_OF_ARTHROPODS, DURABILITY->UNBREAKING, DIG_SPEED->EFFICIENCY, LOOT_BONUS_BLOCKS->FORTUNE, LOOT_BONUS_MOBS->LOOTING, ARROW_DAMAGE->POWER, ARROW_KNOCKBACK->PUNCH, ARROW_FIRE->FLAME, ARROW_INFINITE->INFINITY, PROTECTION_ENVIRONMENTAL->PROTECTION, PROTECTION_FALL->FEATHER_FALLING, OXYGEN->RESPIRATION, WATER_WORKER->AQUA_AFFINITY. Unchanged: MENDING, SILK_TOUCH, FIRE_ASPECT, KNOCKBACK, THORNS.
- `meta.addEnchant(Enchantment.SHARPNESS, 5, true)` (true = ignore level limits) or `item.addUnsafeEnchantment(ench, level)`. Enchantment.getByName and Registry.ENCHANTMENT are deprecated; for config strings use `RegistryAccess.registryAccess().getRegistry(RegistryKey.ENCHANTMENT).get(NamespacedKey.minecraft("sharpness"))` (io.papermc.paper.registry).

## Materials and entity types
- Material.SHORT_GRASS (plain GRASS does not exist), GRASS_BLOCK, CLOCK, PLAYER_HEAD, SPAWNER, TURTLE_SCUTE, ARMADILLO_SCUTE. Chains: Material.CHAIN.
- EntityType: ITEM (not DROPPED_ITEM), FIREWORK_ROCKET, TNT, LIGHTNING_BOLT, SNOW_GOLEM, MOOSHROOM, END_CRYSTAL, EXPERIENCE_ORB, FISHING_BOBBER, ARMOR_STAND. Boats: BOAT, CHEST_BOAT (no per-wood boat types). Thrown potions: POTION.
- Spawning: `world.spawn(loc, Zombie.class, z -> { z.customName(Component.text("Giant", NamedTextColor.RED)); z.setCustomNameVisible(true); })` configures the mob before it appears. Get the killer with `entity.getKiller()` (Player or null).
- `world.setGameRule(GameRule.KEEP_INVENTORY, true)`; GameRule has KEEP_INVENTORY, DO_DAYLIGHT_CYCLE, DO_WEATHER_CYCLE, DO_MOB_SPAWNING, MOB_GRIEFING, FALL_DAMAGE. The String getGameRuleValue/setGameRuleValue are deprecated. Time/weather: world.setTime(1000)/setTime(13000), setStorm(false), setThundering(false).

## Text: Adventure Components (never ChatColor or String setters)
- `Component.text("Hi", NamedTextColor.GREEN)`, `.append(...)`, `.decorate(TextDecoration.BOLD)`; MiniMessage: `MiniMessage.miniMessage().deserialize("<gold>Hi <player>", Placeholder.unparsed("player", name))`. Config text with & codes: `LegacyComponentSerializer.legacyAmpersand().deserialize(s)`. Plain string from a Component: `PlainTextComponentSerializer.plainText().serialize(c)`.
- Send: player.sendMessage(Component), Bukkit.broadcast(Component), player.sendActionBar(Component), player.showTitle(Title.title(main, sub, Title.Times.times(Duration.ofMillis(500), Duration.ofSeconds(3), Duration.ofMillis(500)))). Tab name: player.playerListName(Component). Team prefix: team.prefix(Component).
- Deprecated String APIs (avoid): ChatColor, Bukkit.broadcastMessage, sendTitle(String..), setDisplayName/setPlayerListName/setLore(String), setJoinMessage/setQuitMessage/setDeathMessage, createInventory(holder, size, String), Team.setPrefix(String). Use the Component versions: joinMessage(c), quitMessage(c), deathMessage(c), meta.displayName(c), meta.lore(list).
- Chat: listen to `io.papermc.paper.event.player.AsyncChatEvent` (AsyncPlayerChatEvent is deprecated). `event.message()` / `event.message(Component)`, `event.setCancelled(true)`, `event.renderer((source, displayName, message, viewer) -> ...)`. It runs off the main thread: read only thread-safe data (use a ConcurrentHashMap) and hop back with `Bukkit.getScheduler().runTask(plugin, ...)` before touching players/worlds.

## Commands (the build validates plugin.yml)
- Declare every command in plugin.yml (`commands: name: {description, usage, permission}`) and register with `getCommand("name").setExecutor(handler)` (+ `.setTabCompleter`). Implement `onCommand(CommandSender sender, Command command, String label, String[] args)`; check `if (!(sender instanceof Player player))` for player-only commands; validate args.length and parse numbers inside try/catch. Subcommands: switch on args[0].
- Do not use Brigadier, LifecycleEvents.COMMANDS or JavaPlugin.registerCommand(BasicCommand) (registerCommand does not exist in 1.21.1): the build service only accepts plugin.yml commands.

## Scheduler, threads, data, config
- `Bukkit.getScheduler().runTaskTimer(plugin, () -> {...}, delayTicks, periodTicks)` (20 ticks = 1 s), runTaskLater, runTask; or `new BukkitRunnable(){ public void run(){... cancel(); } }.runTaskTimer(plugin, 0L, 20L)`. Keep the BukkitTask to cancel it. Start a BukkitRunnable with its own runTaskTimer(plugin, ...); passing a BukkitRunnable to the scheduler's runTask*/runTaskTimer throws UnsupportedOperationException at runtime. runTaskAsynchronously only for file IO, never Bukkit API calls. Servers are Paper/Purpur, so do not use the Folia region schedulers. In onDisable save synchronously: once disabling, the scheduler rejects new tasks (IllegalPluginAccessException) and an async save is lost.
- PersistentDataContainer: `NamespacedKey key = new NamespacedKey(plugin, "soulbound")`; `ItemMeta m = item.getItemMeta(); m.getPersistentDataContainer().set(key, PersistentDataType.BOOLEAN, true); item.setItemMeta(m);` then `pdc.has(key, PersistentDataType.BOOLEAN)` / `pdc.get(key, type)` / `getOrDefault`. Types: BYTE, SHORT, INTEGER, LONG, FLOAT, DOUBLE, BOOLEAN, STRING, BYTE_ARRAY, INTEGER_ARRAY, LONG_ARRAY, TAG_CONTAINER, LIST (`PersistentDataType.LIST.strings()`). Players and entities have getPersistentDataContainer() too. (item.editPersistentDataContainer does not exist in 1.21.1; use getItemMeta/setItemMeta.)
- Config: put defaults in src/main/resources/config.yml, call saveDefaultConfig() in onEnable, read with getConfig().getInt("path", def) / getString / getStringList / getConfigurationSection(path) (may be null), reloadConfig() on /x reload. The class is `org.bukkit.configuration.file.FileConfiguration` (NOT org.bukkit.configuration.FileConfiguration).
- Data files: `File f = new File(getDataFolder(), "data.yml"); YamlConfiguration y = YamlConfiguration.loadConfiguration(f); ... y.save(f)` (save throws IOException: catch it). Store per-player data under the UUID string. Locations and ItemStacks can be stored directly: y.set("home", loc), y.getLocation("home"), y.getItemStack("item").

## Events you will commonly need
- Register: `getServer().getPluginManager().registerEvents(listener, this)`; methods annotated `@EventHandler` (optionally `(ignoreCancelled = true, priority = EventPriority.HIGH)`).
- PlayerJoinEvent (player.hasPlayedBefore()), PlayerQuitEvent, PlayerDeathEvent (getPlayer(), getDrops(), getItemsToKeep(), setKeepInventory(bool), deathMessage(Component)), PlayerRespawnEvent (setRespawnLocation), EntityDeathEvent (getEntity().getKiller(), getDrops()), EntityDamageEvent (getCause() == EntityDamageEvent.DamageCause.FALL), EntityDamageByEntityEvent (getDamager() may be a Projectile: check `instanceof Projectile p && p.getShooter() instanceof Player`), BlockBreakEvent, BlockPlaceEvent, PlayerInteractEvent (check `event.getHand() == EquipmentSlot.HAND`, getClickedBlock() may be null), PlayerMoveEvent (fires constantly: use `event.hasChangedBlock()` first), EntityExplodeEvent/BlockExplodeEvent (`blockList().removeIf(...)`).
- TNTPrimeEvent (org.bukkit.event.block): getCause(), getPrimingEntity(), getPrimingBlock(). There is NO getIgnitingEntity().

## Menus (chest GUIs)
- Make a holder class: `class Menu implements InventoryHolder { final Inventory inv = Bukkit.createInventory(this, 27, Component.text("Warps")); public Inventory getInventory(){ return inv; } }` (size a multiple of 9, max 54). Open with player.openInventory(menu.getInventory()).
- In InventoryClickEvent: `if (!(event.getInventory().getHolder(false) instanceof Menu menu)) return; event.setCancelled(true);` then use getRawSlot() (< inventory size = top menu), getCurrentItem() (may be null), isLeftClick()/isRightClick()/isShiftClick(), `event.getWhoClicked()` (cast to Player). Also cancel InventoryDragEvent for menus. Never identify menus by title.

## Items and recipes
- `ItemStack.of(Material.DIAMOND, 5)` or `new ItemStack(mat, n)`. `item.editMeta(meta -> { meta.displayName(Component.text("Super", NamedTextColor.GOLD).decoration(TextDecoration.ITALIC, false)); meta.lore(List.of(Component.text("..."))); meta.setUnbreakable(true); meta.addItemFlags(ItemFlag.HIDE_ENCHANTS); meta.setEnchantmentGlintOverride(true); })`. getItemMeta() is null for AIR. Hand: player.getInventory().getItemInMainHand() (getItemInHand is deprecated); setHelmet(item).
- 1.21.1 has no data-component API (io.papermc.paper.datacomponent does not exist), no ItemMeta.setItemModel/customName/setEquippable; setCustomModelData(Integer) is fine here.
- give items: `player.getInventory().addItem(item)` returns leftovers (HashMap) to drop with world.dropItemNaturally. (Player.give does not exist in 1.21.1.)
- Recipes: `ShapedRecipe r = new ShapedRecipe(new NamespacedKey(plugin, "super_pickaxe"), result); r.shape("DDD", " S ", " S "); r.setIngredient('D', Material.DIAMOND_BLOCK); r.setIngredient('S', Material.STICK); Bukkit.addRecipe(r);` unlock with player.discoverRecipe(key); Bukkit.removeRecipe(key) in onDisable. ShapedRecipe(ItemStack) without a key is deprecated.

## Boss bars and scoreboards
- Adventure boss bar: `BossBar bar = BossBar.bossBar(Component.text("Boss"), 1.0f, BossBar.Color.RED, BossBar.Overlay.PROGRESS); player.showBossBar(bar); bar.progress(f); player.hideBossBar(bar);` progress must stay within 0..1 (clamp it). Colors PINK BLUE RED GREEN YELLOW PURPLE WHITE; overlays PROGRESS, NOTCHED_6/10/12/20. Hide it from everyone when done and in onDisable.
- Sidebar: `Scoreboard sb = Bukkit.getScoreboardManager().getNewScoreboard(); Objective o = sb.registerNewObjective("side", Criteria.DUMMY, Component.text("Title")); o.setDisplaySlot(DisplaySlot.SIDEBAR); o.numberFormat(NumberFormat.blank()); o.getScore("line").setScore(3); player.setScoreboard(sb);` (NumberFormat is io.papermc.paper.scoreboard.numbers.NumberFormat). The registerNewObjective overloads that take a criteria String are deprecated. Score entries must be unique strings (max 15 lines); keep one scoreboard per player and update scores instead of recreating it every tick; reset changed lines with sb.resetScores(entry).

## Main class traps
- JavaPlugin defines final isEnabled(), setEnabled(boolean), getServer(), getDataFolder(), getDescription(), plus getConfig(), saveConfig(), reloadConfig(), getLogger(), getName(), getCommand(). Do not declare methods with those names in your main class (use names like isFeatureOn()).

  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
cd $(q "$WS")
h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)" != "\$h" ]; then

  $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-deps" --max 1800 -- \
      bash -c 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3 && npx prisma generate 2>&1 | tail -1') </dev/null
  echo "\$h" > .devhost-deps
fi
EOF
}

prepare() { init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0; }

REMOTE_UNIT=""
cleanup_remote_unit() {
  if [ -n "$REMOTE_UNIT" ]; then

  fi
}

run_remote() {  # run_remote LOCK MAX CMD...
  local lock="$1" max="$2"; shift 2
  local args=(agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$")
  [ "$lock" = 1 ] && args+=(--lock)
  [ -n "$max" ] && args+=(--max "$max")
  REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$"
  trap cleanup_remote_unit EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP
  local rc=0
  bh_ssh "$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" "${args[@]}" -- "$@")" </dev/null || rc=$?
  REMOTE_UNIT=""
  return $rc
}

cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
case "$cmd" in
  help|-h|--help) sed -n '2,33p' "$0" ;;

  sync)

    GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" git -C "$REPO" push -q --force --prune "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_MIRROR" \
      '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/primary/*' '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
    say "mirror synced ($(git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l) branches)" ;;

  push) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; say "pushed $TOP -> node-2:$WS" ;;
  install) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 1 ;;

  run)
    lock=0; max=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --lock) lock=1; shift ;; --max) max="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "usage: devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD..."
    [ "$lock" = 1 ] && [ -z "$max" ] && max=1500   # keep the shared lock bounded (release builds wait max 30 min)
    prepare
    run_remote "$lock" "$max" "$@" ;;

  tsc)   prepare; run_remote 0 1800 npx tsc --noEmit "$@" ;;
  test)  prepare; if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then run_remote 1 1500 npx tsx --test "$@"; else run_remote 1 1500 bash -c 'npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts'; fi ;;
  build) prepare; run_remote 1 1500 npx next build "$@" ;;

  dev|bg)
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then bname=dev; else bname="${1:?usage: devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...}"; shift; fi

# Cyrus Pattern Library: licensing policy (v1, 2026-10-08)

Applies to every pattern in `services/modbuilder/library/` (all games). The library feeds code into
**customer plugins that customers own, sell and redistribute**, so a pattern's licence must survive
being copied into someone else's closed or commercial jar. That is stricter than "is this open source?".

## 1. The rule in one line

A pattern may only come from (a) code Nxeon writes itself, (b) a Cyrus build whose owner explicitly
opted in, or (c) a third-party source whose licence is on the allow-list below and was **read and
recorded** (SPDX id, URL, commit, attribution text) at ingest time. Everything else is out.

API facts (class names, method signatures, which constant exists in which version) are not code and
are not copyrightable. We take those from the real jars with `javap` (as the version sheets already do),
never from someone's prose or samples.

## 2. Allowed sources

| Source class | SPDX allow-list | Notice in customer output? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nxeon-authored patterns (written fresh for the library, by Nxeon staff or by Cyrus agents working for Nxeon, from API facts only) | `LicenseRef-Nxeon-Authored` | No | **All 30 seed patterns are this class.** |
| Opted-in Cyrus builds (customer gave explicit consent on the listing, section 5) | `LicenseRef-Cyrus-Contributor-Grant` | No (the grant covers reuse) | Designed, not built (needs the owner's ToS wording) |
| No-attribution permissive | `MIT-0`, `0BSD`, `CC0-1.0`, `Unlicense` | No | Allowed. None used for Minecraft yet (Jotunn's `JotunnModExample` is MIT-0, relevant to Valheim) |
| Attribution permissive | `MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `ISC` | **Yes**: the build service writes `META-INF/cyrus-library-NOTICE.txt` into any jar whose build retrieved such a pattern (implemented in `library.js` `noticesFor()`; Apache-2.0 also needs its NOTICE file carried and changes marked) | Allowed with care. None used yet |

## 3. Not allowed (the ingest tool refuses these)

| What | Why |
|---|---|
| Copyleft code: `GPL-*`, `AGPL-*`, `LGPL-*` (copying, not linking), `MPL-2.0` file-level copies, `EPL-*` | Would force the customer's whole plugin under the same licence. Note: **Paper itself is GPL-3.0** (with some MIT-relicensed contributors), so Paper/Bukkit/CraftBukkit *implementation* code is out. Compiling against the Paper API jar, as the service does, is fine and unchanged. |
| ShareAlike content: `CC-BY-SA-*` | ShareAlike would follow the code into customer jars. **Verified 2026-10-08: the PaperMC docs repo (`PaperMC/docs` @ `8ad3909`) is BSD-2-Clause only for its *supporting site code*; the documentation content, including the Java samples inside the `.md` pages, is CC-BY-SA-4.0** (README "License" section). The Adventure docs (`KyoriPowered/adventure-docs`) are CC-BY-SA-4.0 too. So docs samples are **reference only**: read them for understanding, never paste them into a pattern. |
| No licence at all (all rights reserved by default), e.g. `PaperMC/paperweight-test-plugin` (GitHub reports no licence) | No permission to copy. |
| `NOASSERTION` / custom / "free for non-commercial use" / unclear | Ask the author or skip. Customers sell plugins. |
| Bulk scraping or mirroring of Modrinth, CurseForge, SpigotMC, Hangar, Thunderstore, uMod, Steam Workshop or GitHub search | Platform terms forbid automated harvesting for this purpose, and per-project licences vary. Single, hand-picked, licence-checked repos only. |
| Community mods on NxLabs without the author's explicit opt-in | Publishing on NxLabs is not consent to be used as training or pattern material. |
| Decompiled code from any jar (including Mojang, Paper, plugins) | Copyright plus platform EULAs. `javap` signature dumps for API facts are fine. |
| Anything containing secrets, personal data, player names/UUIDs, server IPs | Privacy; also blocked by the safety scan. |

## 4. What every pattern records (enforced by `tools/library.js lint`)

`source.kind` (`nxeon` | `opted-in-build` | `third-party`), `source.license` (SPDX id from the allow-list),
`source.author`, `source.url`, `source.commit` (third-party: exact commit SHA read), `source.retrieved`
(date), `source.attribution` (exact notice text when the licence needs one; empty otherwise),
`source.modified` (true when adapted), `source.notes`. For `opted-in-build`: `source.buildId`,
`source.consentId` and `source.consentAt` instead of URL/commit. The `contentHash` covers code and
metadata, so a changed pattern needs a new review and new verification.

Lint fails when: the SPDX id is not on the allow-list for its kind; a third-party pattern has no URL,
commit or (where required) attribution; an opted-in pattern has no consent id; a pattern contains a
player name/UUID/IP/URL literal; or the code fails the service's own safety scan.

## 5. Customer builds: explicit opt-in, and removal on request

Default is **out**. A build can only become a library pattern when all of these are true:

1. The owner ticked a separate, unticked-by-default box on the listing dialog / NxLabs page:
   "Let Cyrus learn reusable building blocks from this mod (code only, never your name, server or
   players; you can withdraw any time)". Not bundled with publishing, not required for anything.
2. We store a consent record (`LibraryConsent` in `lib/cyrus/library/types.ts`): user id, build id,
   the exact wording version shown, timestamp. No consent record = the miner never sees the build.
3. The miner proposes small, generic blocks (one concern, no customer names, strings or theme),
   normalised to `__PKG__` and placeholder names, and they enter the library as `draft`, never
   directly as `verified`. A human reviewer approves the code and the de-identification.
4. Withdrawal: the owner un-ticks the box (or asks support). Every pattern with that
