## Cyrus Pattern Library: paused as WIP (owner near the usage limit)

The library is built and committed on `feature/cyrus-v6-library` in `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-library`: commit `ebaed875cd`, plus `c4b5dd6288` with the 1.21.4 runtime records. Nothing is deployed, nothing is merged, and VM 88001 was not touched. I used 0 of the 6 allowed real builds: the only way to run the AI is VM 88001's service, and its credential must not be copied anywhere. So every cost and quality number below is an offline model. Unit tests and tsc were not run.

**Library size and verification**
- **Patterns:** 36 Minecraft patterns, all written fresh by Nxeon. They cover all 16 universal categories. 27 are for rarer APIs and can be handed to the model; 9 are common APIs and are only listed, never handed over.
- **Compile and safety scan:** 144 of 144 pattern-version pairs pass (Paper 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11). This ran on node-2 with the service's exact JDK and Paper API classpath, and the service's own safety scan found nothing.
  - That run did not capture compiler warnings. It is fixed but not re-run.
- **Runtime on a real Paper 1.21.4 server:** 32 of 36 pass.
  - One failure is a real bug: `messages` prints `&` colour codes literally when the text also has `<player>` placeholders.
  - Three are wrong assumptions in my own self-tests (`objective-tracker`, `particle-shapes`, `paged-menu`). Paper 1.21.4 still accepts old names like `REDSTONE` and `DROPPED_ITEM`.
  - The runtime check was not run on the other three versions.
- **Result:** no pattern counts as "verified" yet, so the service offers none. It only offers patterns that passed everything on the exact game version.

**Effect on cost and quality (offline model on the 30-prompt eval)**
- **Retrieval switch:** `MB_LIBRARY` is off by default, and off leaves the prompts identical to 0.5.

| Mode | How patterns reach the model | Est. cost per build |
|---|---|---|
| index | list of pattern titles in the cached prompt | +2.1% |
| auto | full code of matching patterns in the request | +7.5% |
| attach | classes placed in the plugin; model sees only their signatures | -0.1% to -4.5%; about -3% on standard and complex builds |

- **Why only attach saves money:** it removes output tokens, the expensive part, instead of adding input. In attach mode the service moves the classes the plugin uses into its package and deletes the rest.
- **Selector:** compared with my labels for the 30 prompts, its picks are 89% correct and it finds 78% of the patterns that would help. The two attack prompts get nothing.
- **First-try pass rate:** not measured. The current eval already passes 28 of 28 first try with no repairs, so there is little to gain there. The real gain is that shipped menus, money, saving and chat code would be the pre-tested versions.

**Licensing decisions the owner must confirm** (in `LICENSING-POLICY.md`)
1. **Seed stays 100% Nxeon-authored.** I checked the PaperMC docs repo directly: its Java samples are CC-BY-SA-4.0, so they cannot go into customers' jars. Paper itself is GPL-3.0, and `paperweight-test-plugin` has no licence at all.
2. **Whether to allow attribution licences** (MIT, Apache, BSD). The service is ready to write a notice file into any customer jar that used such a pattern.
3. **Wording and incentive for the customer opt-in.** The consent record and draft wording exist; the checkbox, the database model and the code that turns builds into patterns do not.

**Recommended next steps** (exact commands in `PAUSED.md`)
1. Run the unit tests, which were never run.
2. Fix the four 1.21.4 failures.
3. Run `verify` again, then `runtime` for all four versions.
4. After the 0.5 deploy, the owner runs the bounded A/B: library off vs attach, about $6.

**New files**
- `lib/cyrus/library/types.ts`
- `lib/cyrus/library/status.ts`
- `services/modbuilder/library.js`
- `services/modbuilder/library/`
- `services/modbuilder/tools/library.js`
- `services/modbuilder/tools/library-env.sh`
- `services/modbuilder/tools/library-ab.js`
- `services/modbuilder/eval/library-labels.json`
- `test/cyrus-library.test.ts`
- `test/cyrus-library-pipeline.test.ts`

**Changed files**
- `services/modbuilder/server.js`
- `services/modbuilder/prompts.js`
- `services/modbuilder/Dockerfile`
- `services/modbuilder/run.sh`
- `services/modbuilder/eval/run_eval.py`
- `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts` (health check now expects image 0.6)
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (new "Cyrus Pattern Library" section)

**Notes**, all in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-v6/library/`:
- `LIBRARY.md`
- `LICENSING-POLICY.md`
- `SCALE-PLAN.md`
- `PAUSED.md`

The node-2 toolchain cache (about 1 GB, gitignored) is still there; `devhost rm` removes it when the work is done.
